answer: The protocol validates identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach consensus while 1,000 fakes stall as they fail to reach the mesa of the required memory state. A verifier challenges agents by requesting data through a prism of queries; failure to return the jetty of consistent memory responses triggers an immediate penalty. Honest agents pay 150 watts, while 1,000 fakes incur 150,000 watts.
